advisory.finding: The skip path uses a plain `echo` while the rest of this workflow surfaces degraded/skipped conditions via GitHub annotations (`::warning::`). When a gate script is absent the step reports fully green with no annotation, so a reviewer or operator cannot tell from the Verified vote or run summary that a (security-adjacent) gate was silently skipped.
advisory.suggested_fix: Change both skip `echo` lines to `echo "::warning::scripts/... not in checked-out tree (change predates the gate) — skipping"`.

docs/architecture.md:282: "CI enforces this with the **raw-git-write gate** (`scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py`, ticket d37e): a raw `subprocess` git mutation ... outside a seam fails the build" — confirms the gate enforces a security invariant

The guard's skip branch exits 0 (fail-open) whenever the file is absent, with no distinction between a predating base and a change that itself removes/renames the script; deleting the script both trips the skip and, post-merge, permanently disables the gate on main.
advisory.finding: The new `if [ -f scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py ]` guard makes the security-relevant raw-git-write gate fail-open: it skips (exit 0) whenever the script is absent, keying only on file existence. It cannot distinguish the intended 'change base predates the gate' case from a change whose tree deletes/renames the gate script — so a change that removes the script silently bypasses the gate on that same change, and after merge the gate is defeated on main.
scenarios: A change deletes or renames scripts/check_raw_git_writes.py in the same commit that adds an unsanctioned raw git write against the tickets store; the gate skips instead of failing.
Post-merge branch CI on main after such a change: the script is gone, so the gate step skips on every subsequent change too.
